summary.headline: Fix the missing governed glossary first — it's the root behind four separate team symptoms.
summary.narrative: Marketing, Sales and Customer Success each report a different surface problem, but three of them trace to one RevOps-level root: there is no governed glossary and no owner of shared definitions. Patch the root before the team-level symptoms. A second root — broken object/handoff integrity — blocks trustworthy AI routing.

roadmap.action: Stand up a governed glossary with a named owner; reconcile MQL/'qualified'/customer first.
roadmap.root_cause: No governed glossary and no owner of shared definitions — every team defines core terms differently.
symptoms: marketing & sales disagree weekly on 'qualified' (deal-update transcript)
MQL flag set inconsistently across lead sources (mkt-audience-consent-readiness)

roadmap.action: Repair object & handoff integrity: orphaned opps, broken lead→opp seams, duplicate accounts.
roadmap.root_cause: No referential-integrity discipline on the lead→opp→case spine, so AI routing can't trust the graph.
symptoms: lead converted to a non-existent opp (revops-data-architecture-handoff)

roadmap.action: Close the consent/identity gaps before any marketing AI touches a contact.
roadmap.root_cause: No shared consent + identity model — consent basis is 'unknown' on a third of MQLs.
symptoms: cold-list leads with no consent record (mkt-audience-consent-readiness)

roadmap.action: Author missing CS grounding articles (rate limits, billing-dispute scope) and a measurement feedback loop.
roadmap.root_cause: No retrieval-readiness or measurement loop to catch AI output degrading before damage spreads.
symptoms: 38% of common intents have no KB article (cs-intent-scope-mapper)
no feedback loop on AI output quality (marketing measurement gap)

cta.line: If you'd like help executing this roadmap, reach out to SaaScend.
